title: Live Probe Harness and Feedback Ingest Specification
author: Maya Chen
content:
Summary

This document specifies the Live Probe Harness and Feedback Ingest pipeline used to collect, transform, and surface targeted production probes for model onboarding, continuous evals, and regression detection. The harness balances three priorities: (1) safe, privacy-preserving capture of representative real-world prompts; (2) rich telemetry and annotation plumbing for automated triage and human review; (3) deterministic routing into eval, retraining, and rollback workflows.

Goals

- Provide a low-friction mechanism to collect small, labeled probe samples from live traffic without impacting customer request latency or privacy guarantees.
- Enable automated tagging and scoring of probes for: quality regressions, quantization sensitivity, function-call/structured-output stability, and latency-cost profiling.
- Ensure probes can be replayed deterministically across model variants and quantization profiles in the eval harness.

Scope and non-goals

- In scope: probe capture sampling rules, ingestion schema, basic enrichment (metadata, anonymization), downstream routing (storage, eval queue, labeler), and SLOs for pipeline availability and freshness.
- Out of scope: labelling UI UX design, long-term annotation storage beyond retention window (see Data Retention), and ML model training pipelines (those consume outputs from this pipeline but are documented separately).

Terminology

- Probe: a single captured request/response example plus telemetry and anonymized context used for evaluation.
- ProbeSet: a curated group of probes assigned to an eval campaign or model onboarding job.
- Ingest Agent: lightweight capture component running in the request path (hosted or private) that emits probe events.

Architecture Overview

1) Ingest Agents: deployed as a sidecar/edge filter within the request path. Agents sample requests according to policy, redact PII client-side, and emit compact probe events to the Ingest Bus.
2) Ingest Bus (Kafka / PubSub): durable, ordered buffer. Events are partitioned by customer_id and model_family to support deterministic replay.
3) Enrichment and Privacy Stage: stream processors that apply static enrichment (token counts, language detection, conversation-turn mapping), PII scrubbing (regex, model-based redaction), and differential-privacy noise injection for customer-sensitive fields when required.
4) Classification and Routing: deduplication, heuristic tagging (latency outlier, function-call, multi-turn), quality-scorer (fast ML model), then route to one or more sinks: Eval Queue, Probe Lake (S3 bucket for long-ish retention), or Immediate Alerting for severe failures.
5) Eval Harness Integration: probes routed to eval queue are materialized into deterministic jobs (seeded RNG, fixed tokenizer) for cross-model replay and scoring.

Probe Lifecycle (high level)

1. Capture: Ingest Agent captures request and response snapshot (configurable sample rate, default 0.1% of requests).
2. Local Redaction: Agent applies PII redaction rules and annotates redaction level.
3. Emit: Event pushed to Ingest Bus with minimal payload (see schema).
4. Enrich: Stream jobs add telemetry and quality signals.
5. Route: Classifier decides sink(s).
4. Consume: Eval harness or labeler consumes event and produces labels/metrics.

Sampling and Capture Policies

- Default global sampling: 0.1% uniform across requests.
- Adaptive sampling: increase for new/under-evaluated prompt clusters, error responses (HTTP 5xx), rate-limited token spikes (response tokens > 2048), or flagged feature usage (function-call).
- Customer opt-out: honor per-customer privacy flags. Agents must not capture when customer config disables live probes.

Ingest Event Schema (compact JSON example)

```json
{
  "probe_id": "uuid-v4",
  "captured_at": "2026-03-05T14:22:10Z",
  "customer_id_hash": "sha256:xxxxx",
  "model_family": "gptx-8k",
  "prompt_tokens": 42,
  "response_tokens": 128,
  "lang": "en",
  "redaction_level": "pii-scrubbed",
  "latency_ms": 132,
  "http_status": 200,
  "metadata": {"route":"chat-completion","feature_flags":["function_call"]},
  "payload_ref": "s3://probe-lake/2026/03/05/probe-uuid.json"
}
```

Note: For this Confluence doc we show payload_ref rather than embedding full text to limit bus bandwidth. The payload stored in Probe Lake is encrypted and access-controlled.

Privacy and Safety Controls

- PII Redaction: On-agent regex + model heuristics. Redaction policy documented separately in privacy-playbook.
- Customer Opt-out: honor explicit per-customer settings; default is opt-in for accounts created after 2025-06-01.
- DP Noise: for high-sensitivity customers tagging, the Enrichment stage can apply Laplace noise to numeric telemetry fields when flagged.
- Access Controls: RBAC enforced for Probe Lake (read restricted to SRE/Applied ML/product with justification).

SLOs and Metrics

- Ingest availability: 99.95% monthly.
- End-to-end freshness (capture -> Eval queue readiness): P99 < 2 minutes for non-sampled burst probes; default P95 < 30s for steady-state.
- Successful enrichment rate (no processing errors): 99.0%.

Monitoring signals to emit

- probe.capture.rate by model_family and customer_tier
- probe.enrich.failure.count and top error types
- pipeline.latency.{p50,p95,p99}
- probe.privacy.violations (alerts if redaction fails)

Probe Promotion and Onboarding Flow (how probes are used)

1. Curator or automation selects ProbeSet candidates based on tags (e.g., quant-sensitive candidates have token-length > 2048 or high perplexity).
2. Offline eval jobs replay probes across: baseline model, candidate model, quantized variant(s). Comparison outputs are stored and scored by automated metrics: semantic-similarity, prefix-consistency, function-call fidelity, hallucination score.
3. If automated pass, probe set moves to a human labeling batch for edge-case review.
4. Pass/fail gates feed into a Promotion Decision: green = promote variant to canary; amber = create targeted retrain or prompt-rewrite; red = reject.

Operational Playbook (fast triage steps)

1. Alert: probe.enrich.failure spike or pipeline.latency.p99 breach.
2. Page on-call for Ingest pipeline.
3. Run diagnostics: check Ingest Bus consumer lags, inspect last successful offset, run sample enrichment job locally against sample payload_ref.
4. If corruption found in payloads, isolate offending partition and trigger synthetic replays.
5. If PII redaction failure rate increased, suspend live capture (flip config flag) and notify privacy on-call.

Example CLI recipes

- Re-run enrichment for a batch of probes:

```bash
probe-tool reprocess --from 2026-03-01T00:00:00Z --to 2026-03-01T01:00:00Z --topic ingest-enrich --dry-run
```

- Create ProbeSet manifest for eval harness:

```yaml
name: quant-sensitivity-run-2026-03-06
probes: # list of probe_id strings
  - uuid-1
  - uuid-2
seed: 94107
variants: ["gptx-8k", "gptx-8k-quant8"]
```

Annotation and Labeling Contract

- Label schema: flat list of tags and numeric calibration scores. Example fields: {"coherence": [0-1], "hallucination": [0-1], "function_call_correct": {true|false|n/a}, "severity": [P0|P1|P2|P3]}.
- Label provenance must include labeler_id, label_timestamp, and probe_snapshot_ref.

Data Retention and Access

- Probe Lake retention default: 90 days. Business justification required for extensions.
- Probe metadata in event store retained for 365 days.
- Audit logs for access to Probe Lake retained for 1 year.

Failure Modes and Mitigations

- Upstream high-volume customer producing many probes: apply per-customer sampling caps and backpressure at Ingest Agent.
- Enrichment pipeline consumer lag: autoscale consumers and open an investigation runbook that includes backlog replay steps.
- Privacy regression (PII escapes): immediate suspend capture for affected clusters, initiate privacy incident playbook.

Ownership and Contacts

- Primary owner: Applied ML — Probe Infrastructure (team: applied-ml-probe).
- Secondary: Runtime telemetry (team: eng-serving-runtime).
- On-call rotation: probe-infra-oncall@redwood.internal (see eng-platform/oncall roster).

Open TODOs and Future Work

- Integrate active learning loop to prioritize probes where model disagreement is highest.
- Add pre-ingest differential-privacy guarantees for entire dataset exports.
- Expose a limited customer-facing preview of probes for customers who opt-in to feedback.

- Serving simulation harness: /applied-ml-and-evals/eval-harness/serving-simulation-eval-harness-2026

Appendix: Quick config table

| Config key | Default | Description | Owner |
|-----------|---------|-------------|-------|
| ingest.sample_rate.global | 0.001 | Global uniform sampling fraction | applied-ml-probe |
| ingest.sample_rate.max_per_customer | 0.01 | Per-customer cap to avoid noisy customers | applied-ml-probe |
| ingest.redaction.mode | pii-scrubbed | Levels: none | pii-scrubbed | dp-noise | applied-ml-probe |
| retention.probe_lake_days | 90 | Days before probe payloads are expired | eng-platform |
